title: App execution context: CLR, WinForms, App worker and timing worker
scope: Static App entry, mixed-mode CLR transition, WinForms event registration, native worker dispatch, pause and shutdown. Complete captured bodies do not establish full transitive semantics, live scheduling or exclusive ownership of all Actor writers.
result: The normal outer App execution path is closed through real PE/CLR metadata, WinForms event registration, native thread creation and concrete virtual-slot binding. Gameplay App updates run on the registered App worker; UI and timing work have separate contexts. Exclusive ownership of every Actor/STATUS write and complete shutdown recovery remain unproved.
limitations: No target execution, attachment, injection, window interaction, IDB modification, save or product modification.
CLR metadata/IL inventory is separate from native coverage and is not 439 new semantic claims. Twenty-one selected managed bodies support this context study.
Two discontiguous functions are captured with six exact byte chunks and complete IDA pagination; they are not mislabeled as contiguous coverage bodies.
Native caller xrefs alone miss CLR MethodDef transitions and are not a complete indirect-call census. Original pointers are not live immutable bindings.
The optional timing callback at device+728, input/UI callbacks, external CLR/WinForms implementation, CRT initializers/TLS, and all transitive GPU/resource failure paths are not exhaustively closed.
Pause+776 is a request/state flag with timing-thread behavior, not a lock, worker drain or Actor/STATUS ownership lease.
The existing task/fiber evidence still permits parked child stacks; knowing the registered App worker does not collapse those stack lifetimes.
GetExitCodeThread failure, invalid/closed/reused handles, repeated init, exception exits and synchronous UI invocation races are not proven safe by the normal shutdown path.
trainerConsequences: Use the concrete App-worker dispatch chain as provenance for a future native command gate; separately validate live module/object/vtable identity and initialization state.
Do not execute arbitrary gameplay writes directly in WinForms callbacks or on an injected worker based on a generic main-thread label.
Do not treat minimize/pause, a posted exit flag, a quiet active OS stack, or a closed HANDLE as Actor-lifetime quiescence.

Any future Actor provider still requires actual binding/lifetime serialization, suspended-fiber accounting and closure of relevant worker writers. This research alone enables no installer, IPC or gameplay feature.
